S.title: Map What Could Change - Community Builders of Pecan Grove
S.intro1: The plan for the farm is posted. The Planning Board meets soon.
S.intro2: Each change makes ripples, like a stone in a pond. Follow them, near and far.
q: Where does it land first? Tap a place.
Who could feel it next? Tap a neighbor.
wrong: Good thinking. It may get there later, but look for where it lands first. Try once more.
Good thinking. It may reach them a little, but look for who feels it most. Try once more.
shown: Here is where it can land.
Here is who it can reach.
S.end: Look how far the changes went!
S.can: I can look for changes far from the building, too.
S.tip100: Great map! Try a new round with new changes.
S.tipHelp: Next time, follow the helpful changes as far as the hard ones.
S.tipHard: Next time, follow the hard changes as far as the helpful ones.

$parts: ' all the way: where it lands first, and who lives or works there.

S.tipStep2: Next time, ask: who lives, works or plays near that place?
S.tipPaths: Next time, follow the dotted paths far from the farm.
S.real: With a grown-up, draw a map of your neighborhood. Mark places a big new building could change, both helpful and hard.
S.guText: Some effects land far from the site: power bills, rents, school budgets, a creek downstream, or the roads school buses use. Kids follow each change to where it lands, whether it helps or is hard. Helpful and hard changes are worth the same points, which keeps the game balanced.

bank.b0011: Taxes from the building can help pay for the school and the town.
bank.b0012: Jayden could get new classes, and Grandma Ruth could pay less tax on her home.
bank.b0014: Building crews eat and shop on Main Street.
bank.b0015: Mr. Patel gets more customers and could hire more people.
bank.b0016: Building jobs for a year or two
bank.b0017: Paychecks from the building crew come home to Pecan Grove families.
bank.b0018: Mrs. Ana could get more work, and Grandma Ruth's grandson could find a job.
bank.b0020: The school could add classes for building and power jobs.
bank.b0021: Mrs. Ana could teach, and Jayden could learn a trade and work here someday.
bank.b0022: A fast internet line comes to town
bank.b0023: The fiber line to the building could also reach the clinic and homes.
bank.b0024: Ms. Lee could do video visits, and Grandma Ruth could video-call her family.
bank.b0025: The plan fixes the farm road
bank.b0026: A smoother road leads from the farm to Main Street and the clinic.
bank.b0027: Mr. Johnson's crops get to the store easily, and ambulances reach Ms. Lee's clinic fast.
bank.b0028: Big water use on hot days
bank.b0029: On hot days, keeping the computers cool can use a lot of water from wells and the river.
bank.b0030: Mr. Johnson's cows and well, and Ms. Lee's clinic, need water too.
bank.b0032: When rain hits bare dirt, mud can wash into the creek, the Pecan River and nearby wells.
bank.b0033: Mr. Johnson's well and Mrs. Ana's fishing spot are downstream.
bank.b0035: Trucks fill Main Street and the roads that school buses and ambulances use.
bank.b0036: Mr. Patel's shoppers, Jayden's bus and Ms. Lee's ambulances could all take longer for months.
bank.b0038: Lights that stay on all night can shine into nearby homes.
bank.b0039: Mr. Johnson lives next door, and Ms. Lee and Jayden's little sister want dark nights.
bank.b0040: Many workers need places to live
bank.b0041: Rents for homes and shops near Main Street can go up for a while.
bank.b0042: Mr. Patel rents his shop, and Mrs. Ana rents her home.
bank.b0043: The building needs lots of power
bank.b0044: New power lines cost money, and power bills for homes and shops can change.
bank.b0045: Grandma Ruth and Mr. Patel keep a close eye on their power bills.
